details: The broader cryptocurrency market has experienced a significant downturn, with Bitcoin falling below $76,000 and showing a trend towards its fifth consecutive weekly loss. This market movement is largely attributed to a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks and considerable outflows from US-listed Bitcoin spot Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), triggering widespread liquidations across the crypto ecosystem.
title: Crypto Markets Face Broad Sell-off, Bitcoin Dips Below $76K

details: Ethereum's price has fallen more sharply than Bitcoin's in the last 24 hours, dropping approximately 7.9% to around $2,237. This intensified decline is linked to the broader tech stock crash, which also impacted Bitcoin, and a reversal in US spot Ether ETF inflows. The drop has pushed ETH to its lowest daily levels since mid-August.
title: Ethereum Suffers Steeper Decline Than Bitcoin Amid ETF Outflows

details: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Federal Reserve Board have officially withdrawn their proposal to reduce the reporting threshold for cross-border cryptocurrency transfers from $3,000 to $250. This decision comes after receiving nearly 3,000 public comments, with the majority expressing opposition due to concerns over increased compliance costs for smaller institutions and potential privacy risks.
title: US Regulators Withdraw Proposal for Lower Crypto Transfer Reporting Threshold

details: Solana's price has plummeted below the $90 mark, trading around $89.62, representing a more than 7% decrease in the last 24 hours. The decline is part of a broader crypto market sell-off. Concurrently, Anza, the development team behind Solana's Agave validator client, has issued a mandatory call for all mainnet validators to upgrade to version 4.4.1 by November 6, 2026, to ensure compatibility with the canonical chain.
title: Solana Price Plummets Below $90; Mandatory Validator Upgrade Underway
